title: Reversible infrastructure mutation
subtitle: Edits that touch several services happen in one rollback-protected transaction, and every create has a symmetric delete. The function generator is the worked example.
lede: FAFO Core and Function Forge lets an agent add a function to a working multi-service estate, and I wanted every such change to be undoable exactly. Creating a function adds a crate and edits four other parts of the estate in one operation. Each edit runs through an atomic file layer with its own rollback per integration, so a failure halfway leaves the estate as it was and a function cannot end up registered in one service and missing from another. I built the exit path with the entry path. The generator writes every edit at a known landmark in its target file, and delete finds those landmarks and reverses each edit, which makes reversal exact.
quote: I design changes to a working system so they can be undone exactly, and I put the human decision on the one step where undo stops being free.
evidence: Reversible infrastructure changes: a function generator whose edits across five parts of a multi-service estate run through one atomic file layer with rollback.
Code generation with exact undo: every generated edit anchored at a landmark so delete reverses it exactly, and regeneration over a developer zone refused unless forced.
Human-in-the-loop operations: build and restart separated, so every automated step can be repeated or undone and the restart is the one human step.
author: Corey James
